title: What WooCommerce plugin to build next
subtitle: An expertise-mode scout for a PHP/WooCommerce plugin developer: categories where stores already pay but complain, or where a plugin was abandoned or repriced.

verdict.summary: The loudest verified pain is product catalog sync to Meta and Google on large WooCommerce stores. The official plugins are rated 2.1 and 2.7 on WordPress.org, and reviews from different authors describe sync jobs that crash servers or stall. But a catalog-sync plugin isn't an open gap: CTX Feed markets itself for large catalogs, WebToffee already ships batched, scheduled Meta sync, and Google can crawl the store for free, so it scores 61 and fails GO. The pivot is a sync-health monitor that works alongside existing sync plugins, not another feed generator. Test that before writing much code.

opportunities.name: Throttled catalog sync for large-catalog stores (Meta + Google)
opportunities.one_liner: Batched, observable product sync that doesn't take down a 10k+ SKU store.
opportunities.why: Pain 8: recent reviews from different authors across three vendors describe sync overloading big servers or stalling (e1, e2, e4, e5, e6), plus silent sync failures (e10-e14). WTP 6: stores pay for feed plugins (e40) and complain about license and refund terms (e19, e20, e23), not about paying. But official sync is free (e42). Gap 4: well-rated paid alternatives exist and switchers name them (e24-e27); CTX markets large catalogs (e46) and WebToffee ships batch and scheduled Meta sync (e48, e49), though CTX admits big catalogs break feeds (e47). Fit 7: core Woo/PHP work, but Meta API review is a stretch. Reach 5: the only verified gathering place is the WordPress.org forums, which ban self-promotion (e51). Build 5: an MVP takes weeks, reliability at 50k SKUs takes months.

opportunities.name: Product add-ons / custom options plugin
opportunities.one_liner: Another product options and price-calculator plugin.
opportunities.why: Stores pay (official Product Add-Ons is $79/yr, e44) and complain about price jumps (e28) and broken add-on pricing (e30). But most PPOM complaints are 5 to 10 years old (e29, e30, e31), and well-loved cheap alternatives exist: ThemeHigh Extra Product Options is 4.9/5 with only 5 one-star reviews out of 219, and Advanced Product Fields is 4.8/5 (WordPress.org API). wc-kalkulator was closed on 2026-06-21 for a security issue, but it was small.

opportunities.name: Booster for WooCommerce lifetime-holder replacement
opportunities.one_liner: Replace the modules repriced away from lifetime buyers.
opportunities.why: Lifetime buyers lost support when it moved to $129.99/yr (e32, e33, e34). The complaints come from one vendor and are mostly 2 to 5 years old. The buyers are hard to find, and Booster has 100+ modules to match.

gap.statement: WooCommerce stores with thousands of products that sell through Facebook/Instagram and Google Shopping can't keep their catalog in sync without stalling or overloading their server, because the official plugins run heavy, unthrottled sync jobs, and the paid feed plugins that claim to handle large catalogs still draw "feed gets stuck" complaints.

pains.theme: Sync overloads the server or stalls on big catalogs
pains.summary: Catalog/feed jobs crash servers with 24 to 32 GB of RAM, or get stuck partway through.
Setup says it's connected, but products never appear and nobody can explain why.

pains.theme: Sync tied to ad accounts, with suspensions
pains.summary: Store owners want catalog sync without the ads account, and suspensions block selling.
License changes, refused refunds, and updates that rewrite feed settings.
Price jumps, features moved to paid add-ons, broken add-on pricing (mostly old).
Booster lifetime buyers lost support when it became a paid yearly plan.

critic.rebuttal: No shut-down or postmortem of a WooCommerce catalog-sync plugin was found.

critic.risk: Free incumbent: Google Merchant Center can crawl the store daily with no plugin (e50), and Meta can pull a scheduled feed URL.
Already exists and copyable: CTX markets large catalogs (e46), and WebToffee ships per-batch and scheduled Meta sync (e48, e49). The only edge left is execution quality.
Channel closed: WordPress.org forums ban self-promotion (e51), and the woocommerce.com marketplace is gated.
Meta API approval (business verification, app review) for direct sync
critic.rebuttal: Hosted feed URLs need no app review, but that turns the product into another feed generator (see the previous risk). The pivot reads job status locally and avoids the issue.

critic.risk: Pain is real but nobody pays
critic.rebuttal: Stores already pay for feed plugins (e40) and complain about terms, not about paying (e19, e23).

win_plan.positioning: Know when Facebook or Google stopped showing your products, before your sales tell you.

pricing.recommendation: Unvalidated; test $49 to $79/yr per site after the 7-day check
pricing.rationale: Stores already pay feed vendors, but official sync is free. The price has to sit below a feed-plugin licence.

validation.experiment: Ship a free, read-only sync-health check and answer 15 open WordPress.org sync-failure threads with real diagnostics (no links).
validation.pass_bar: 10 stores run the check and 3 ask for paid alerts
steps: Day 1-2: build a read-only check of Action Scheduler failures for the Meta and Google plugins
Day 3-5: answer 15 open sync threads with diagnostics, no links
Day 6-7: invite people from your own site or blog, then count runs and paid asks

kill_criteria: Fewer than 5 stores run the check in 7 days
Stores say the sync plugin's own logs and Merchant Center diagnostics are enough
